description.value: We directly compared reappraisal and distraction using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to investigate common and distinct neural mechanisms of emotion regulation.

spans.text: We, therefore, directly compared distraction and reappraisal using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

value: We hypothesized that both active task conditions downregulate amygdala activity but that the neural networks subserving this regulation differ for reappraisal and distraction.
Common network nodes should include regions in the dlPFC and dmPFC, as well as inferior parietal sites.

In contrast, OFC activation should be observed for reappraisal only, whereas distraction should yield activation specific to attentional control and task-related activity in mainly superior parietal sites.
Contrasting the connectivity patterns of the amygdala during reappraisal and distraction should corroborate these neural networks.
